deep.reconstruction:
This page is a combinatorial pants decomposition of maps (cartes, i.e. dessins / ribbon graphs). It continues p.65, 'Découpage de cartes en pantalons généralisés'.

(1) Local model, the weighted triangle. Take a topological pair of pants whose three holes form a set J = {0, 1, ∞}. Subdivide it 'in standard fashion': every edge is an arc running between two different holes. Such a subdivision is determined up to isotopy by a 'weighted triangle' π: J → N. Here π(j) is the number of arcs joining the two holes other than j.
- The worked example has α = 3 arcs a_i between 1 and ∞, β = 5 arcs b_i between 0 and ∞, and γ = 4 arcs c_i between 0 and 1.
- It is drawn both as the annulus picture with holes 0 and 1 inside the outer circle ∞, with points a^0, b^0, a^1, b^1, a^∞, b^∞ on the boundary circles, and as a triangle with vertices 0, 1, ∞ and the arcs marked as ticks on its sides.
- The number of marked points on the three cuffs is α' = β+γ, β' = γ+α, γ' = α+β, so α'+β'+γ' = 2(α+β+γ).
- Inverting: α = (β'+γ'−α')/2 = (α'+β'+γ')/2 − α', and cyclically for β and γ.
- He notes that given cuff counts α', β', γ' are realisable iff α'+β'+γ' is even.
- The cyclic order of points on a cuff is the circular concatenation of the intervals [1,α] and [1,β]; this is the marginal sketch '[α][1,β]' and the sequence 'c1 c2 c3 c4 . b5 b4 b3 b2 b1'.

(2) Global statement. An oriented map cut 'pantalonnement' in standard fashion is equivalent to a 'generalised pants graph'. This is a cellular, oriented trivalent graph, dual to the pants decomposition, which may also have univalent vertices ('uni-points d'ordre 1'): degenerate pieces where a cuff shrinks to a vertex or face of the map. It carries three kinds of data:
- Weights on the corners (vertex s, incident edge) giving each piece its weighted triangle.
- A compatibility condition along each edge s–t: α_s+β_s = α'_t+β'_t = γ, the common number of points on the shared cuff.
- For each edge, an anti-bijection between the two Z/γ-torsors. Each torsor is the circular sum of [1,α_s] and [1,β_s] (respectively [1,α'_t] and [1,β'_t]). It is 'anti' because the gluing reverses orientation.
This is a discrete analogue of Fenchel–Nielsen / Dehn–Thurston coordinates for maps. The cuff intersection numbers play the role of lengths, and the torsor identification (a twist mod γ) plays the role of the twist. The large pencil sketch shows a trivalent graph with labels A_{0∞}, A_{01}, A_{10}, A_{1∞}, A_{∞1}, A_{∞0} for the six corner/edge types of a pair of pants.

(3) Counting check. Collapse each hole of the standard pants to a point. This gives a map on the sphere with three vertices 0, 1, ∞ and α+β+γ edges (bundles of α, β, γ parallel arcs). Its faces are (α−1)+(β−1)+(γ−1) bigons plus 2 triangles, so α+β+γ−1 faces. Euler: 3 − (α+β+γ) + (α+β+γ−1) = 2. The right column describes the dual picture in terms of orders α', β', γ'.
errors: The realisability criterion is incomplete. Parity of α'+β'+γ' is not enough: α = (β'+γ'−α')/2 ≥ 0 also needs the triangle inequalities α' ≤ β'+γ', β' ≤ γ'+α', γ' ≤ α'+β'. When a triangle inequality fails, a standard subdivision does not exist and arcs returning to the same cuff are needed. This is exactly what the 'non-standard' pieces / generalised pants must handle.
Minor slip in the definition: π(j) should count edges joining the two holes other than j ('qui relient i et k'), not 'j et k' as written.

In the gluing data, the edge condition is stated for cuff counts, but the indexing (γ = γ'_s = γ'_t versus α_s+β_s) is notationally inconsistent on the page. The intended meaning — equal cuff counts on both sides — is clear.

ideas.what: A standard (arc-only) subdivision of a pair of pants is classified by a weighted triangle (α, β, γ); cuff counts are α' = β+γ etc., inverted by half-differences with a parity condition
ideas.modern_name: Dehn–Thurston / normal-arc coordinates of a multiarc in a pair of pants; integral combinatorial pants ribbon graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn (1922, unpublished until later); Thurston (1970s); Penner–Harer, Combinatorics of Train Tracks (1992)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses pants decompositions and the Teichmüller tower qualitatively, but not these formulas

ideas.what: Equivalence: a map cut in standard pants fashion ↔ a trivalent (plus univalent) graph with corner weights, edge compatibility α_s+β_s = α'_t+β'_t, and an anti-bijection of Z/γ-torsors (discrete twist) on each edge
ideas.modern_name: Discrete Fenchel–Nielsen / Dehn–Thurston coordinates for integral ribbon graphs (maps); combinatorial Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn–Thurston coordinates for multicurves (Dehn, Thurston, Penner); combinatorial Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates for metric ribbon graphs: Andersen–Borot–Charbonnier–Giacchetto–Lewański–Wheeler (2020)

ideas.what: Cyclic set of points on a cuff as a Z/γ-torsor obtained by circular concatenation of [1,α] and [1,β]; gluing is an orientation-reversing torsor identification
ideas.modern_name: Twist parameter mod γ / cyclic gluing data

ideas.what: Collapsed standard pants as a map on P^1 with three vertices 0, 1, ∞, with face count (α−1)+(β−1)+(γ−1) bigons + 2 triangles, checked by Euler

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a pants-decomposition coordinate system for maps/dessins. Each pair of pants is a 'weighted triangle' determined by its cuff counts (parity condition), and the pieces are glued by Z/γ-torsor anti-isomorphisms (discrete twists). This anticipates combinatorial Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates on combinatorial Teichmüller space and pants-based lattice-point counts of ribbon graphs/maps. Those are usually dated to the 2010s–2020s (Norbury lattice counts; Andersen–Borot–Charbonnier–Giacchetto–Lewański–Wheeler 2020), and the literature does not trace them to Grothendieck's 1983 dessin-oriented notes.
missed.quote: Carte orientée découpée pantalonnement de façon standard ⟷ ... avec une pondération ... α_s+β_s = α'_t+β'_t ... et de la donnée d'une anti-bijection des torseurs sous Z/α_s
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows the pants-decomposition (Teichmüller tower / Lego) viewpoint of the Esquisse was being made quantitative on maps themselves. This gives a discrete Dehn–Thurston parametrisation of dessins, of the kind now used in topological/geometric recursion and Masur–Veech volume counts. The 'generalised pants' with univalent vertices are a hint at how he meant to handle degenerate cuffs.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is essentially integral Dehn–Thurston coordinates transposed to maps, which a specialist would recognise as classical. What is notable is the explicit dessin/map formulation with torsor gluing data in 1983, close to the modern combinatorial Fenchel–Nielsen picture. It is not a new theorem, and the criterion even omits the triangle inequalities.
transcription_corrections: 'un ens J de trans' should read 'un ens J de trous' (holes).
'π(j) = nb d'arêtes qui relient j et k' — intended (and probably written) as edges joining the two holes other than j.
'quelle pantalonnière généralisée' is uncertain; possibly 'graphe pantalonnier généralisé' or similar.
Bottom-right 'α+β+γ bigones' under 'trois sommets' is more likely 'α+β+γ arêtes' (edges); bigons appear on the next line.
Right column ('2 sommets d'ordre α',β',γ'', '= α+β+γ−2', 'α+β+γ−1 faces') is partly illegible. It likely describes the dual configuration in terms of orders α', β', γ' and counts α+β+γ−1.
